design.decision: On every trick, choose between following suit and trumping, so trumps go where they win the most; low [♠]s become live winners.
design.opponent: Revealed the first time the team trumps while holding the led suit; opponents can no longer count on a long suit running and should lead [♠] to strip trumps.
design.rationale: It changes who wins tricks directly and visibly, which the brief asks for. The option-style commons failed because their freedoms rarely mattered, while trumping at will matters on most tricks. The hook is a general card filter on the existing anySuit rule, not per-sigil code.
design.draftText: Your team can play [♠]s even when it can follow suit
design.hooks: anySuit gains an optional card filter (`card`). With it, your team may play a matching card from another suit even when it can follow suit, on every trick, or only inside an existing first/last window when one is also given. Leading [♠] before [♠]s are broken stays illegal, and ordinary trump priority applies.

critic.concerns: Lifting follow-suit for [♠] is a big rule change, and opponents can no longer run long suits, but it is visible once used.
